findings.title: Zero set-aside buffer on the sDOLA destination departs from story 091 Decision 6 / story 082 Phase 4 with no authorising story
findings.description: Story 091 L97 and Decision 6 (L195-197) say: 'V2's buffer pct on the destination = V1's pct read from the source in Phase 0'. Story 082 L73 (Phase 4) says setSetAsideBuffer(v2, <value read from V1>), and 082 L172 expects DOLA 10. Commit 1349be8 has no [story-NNN] tag. It makes _targetBufferPct return 0 whenever the destination is the sDOLA strategy, and Phase 4, Phase 8 and the verifier assert 0. No story anywhere in ~/code/product-owner/stories/phStaging2 (all states and sprints, latest 097) records this decision. Stories 091 and 082 are auto-complete, so the story tree still describes a 10% DOLA buffer.
findings.impact: No security impact. Law 1 favours the change: the fork harness shows the V2 position on the sDOLA strategy cannot go below par without an owner emergencyWithdraw, so a 10% pct would only have diverted about 10% of DOLA yield into an idle pile that only rescueERC20 can recover. The impact is traceability: the authoritative spec and the shipped script disagree. A later reviewer grading against story 091 would call the zero a defect, and one reading the code would call the story wrong.
findings.recommendation: Record the decision in a story, either as an amendment to 091 Decision 6 or as a new story that cites the monotonicity argument and the zero-buffer rationale. Keep the code as is.
findings.evidence: Story files: 091 L97, L195-197; 082 L73, L172. Commit 1349be8 has no tag. The project fork test test_fork_fullPreview_v2DolaLandsInSdolaStrategy asserts source pct > 0 and destination pct == 0 (PASS).
findings.reconciliation: No fingerprint match. findings.title: With V2's sDOLA set-aside buffer at 0, initiateMigration's balance-measured R has no idle top-up, so a future V2 terminal migration off the sDOLA strategy can realise R a few wei below P from floored share redemption
findings.workingClass: QA / informational: wei-scale rounding. Reasoned from source, not measured.
findings.description: StableStakerV2.initiateMigration sets R = min(balanceOf(this), P) after the strategy exit, so any set-aside buffer, dust or donations absorb a below-par exit before users are haircut. This is the audit-14 ss14l8 softening, cited in-source at ~L832-836. The cutover (1349be8) sets V2's buffer pct on the sDOLA destination to 0 via _targetBufferPct. With no idle pile, when V2's DOLA pool is terminally migrated, the floored share-to-asset conversion in the sDOLA strategy's _disposeShares redeem can return a few wei under booked principal. R < P then scales every user credit by R/P, and floors each credit.
findings.impact: Wei-scale loss spread across DOLA stakers at a future V2 migration. It does not occur in this cutover. No exploit path and nothing an attacker can steer. It is the same loss a small buffer would have absorbed, and it is traded against the ~10% of yield idled by a non-zero buffer (see R37-CUT-01).
findings.recommendation: No code change needed. Optionally document in the story that records the zero-buffer decision (R37-CUT-01) that DOLA migrations lose sub-cent rounding dust with no cushion, or seed a nominal idle top-up before a future initiateMigration.
findings.evidence: StableStakerV2.sol initiateMigration R computation (balance-measured, capped at P). CutoverStableStakerV2Mainnet.s.sol L2102-2105 returns 0 for the sDOLA destination. Not measured on a fork.
